tips.headline: Use @-mentions to give Claude Code precise file context
tips.summary: Boris Cherny, creator of Claude Code, recommends using @-mentions to point Claude at specific files instead of letting it search. This dramatically reduces token usage and improves accuracy since Claude works with the exact files you intend rather than guessing from project structure.
actionable_steps: Type @ in Claude Code to see a file picker with fuzzy search
Select the specific files relevant to your task before writing your prompt
Combine multiple @-mentions for cross-file tasks like refactoring

tips.headline: Write a CLAUDE.md file to set project conventions once
tips.summary: Adding a CLAUDE.md to your project root lets you define coding standards, test commands, and architectural decisions that persist across every Claude Code session. Think of it as onboarding documentation that Claude reads automatically — you teach it once instead of repeating yourself.
actionable_steps: Create a CLAUDE.md in your project root with build/test/lint commands
Add coding conventions like naming patterns, preferred libraries, and file structure
Include architectural decisions and constraints Claude should respect
Use /init in Claude Code to auto-generate a starter CLAUDE.md

tips.headline: Use Claude's extended thinking for complex architectural decisions
tips.summary: When asking Claude to make non-trivial design choices — like choosing between patterns, structuring a new module, or planning a migration — enabling extended thinking produces significantly better results. Claude will reason through trade-offs before committing to an approach, catching issues that quick responses miss.
actionable_steps: For architecture questions, ask Claude to 'think through the trade-offs' explicitly
Use Claude Code's plan mode (shift+tab) for multi-step tasks that need careful reasoning
Review Claude's reasoning in extended thinking to catch flawed assumptions early

sources.title: Tips for getting better architectural advice from Claude

tips.headline: Enable PowerShell tool for Windows development workflows
tips.summary: Claude Code now includes an opt-in PowerShell tool that allows Windows users to execute PowerShell commands directly through Claude. This provides native Windows command-line access for system administration and development tasks.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to version 2.1.84 or later
Enable the PowerShell tool in your settings as a preview feature
Visit https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#powershell-tool for configuration details

tips.headline: Configure streaming timeout for better connection handling
tips.summary: The new CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable lets you customize how long Claude Code waits before timing out idle streaming connections. This helps prevent unnecessary disconnections during long-running operations.
actionable_steps: Set the CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable
Choose a timeout value in milliseconds (default is 90000 for 90 seconds)
Restart Claude Code for the setting to take effect

tips.headline: Use managed settings drop-in directory for team policy deployment
tips.summary: The new managed-settings.d/ directory allows multiple teams to deploy independent configuration fragments that automatically merge. This enables better organization of team-specific policies without conflicts.
actionable_steps: Create a managed-settings.d/ directory alongside your managed-settings.json
Place individual team policy files in the directory (they merge alphabetically)
Name files with prefixes to control merge order (e.g., 01-team-a.json, 02-team-b.json)

tips.headline: Use environment variables to configure MCP server settings in Claude Code
tips.summary: Claude Code v2.1.85 introduced CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME and CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL environment variables for MCP headersHelper scripts. This allows a single helper script to serve multiple MCP servers, simplifying configuration management.
actionable_steps: Set the CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME environment variable to your desired server name
Set the CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL environment variable to your MCP server URL
Update your MCP headersHelper scripts to use these variables instead of hardcoded values

tips.headline: Add session tracking header for proxy aggregation
tips.summary: Use the `X-Claude-Code-Session-Id` header in your API requests to help proxies group requests by session without needing to parse request bodies. This improves routing and monitoring capabilities when using Claude Code through proxy servers.
actionable_steps: Add the `X-Claude-Code-Session-Id` header to your Claude Code API requests
Set the header value to your session identifier
Configure your proxy to use this header for request aggregation instead of body parsing

tips.headline: Set CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1 to eliminate screen flickering
tips.summary: This environment variable enables flicker-free alt-screen rendering with virtualized scrollback in Claude Code v2.1.88+. It provides a smoother visual experience when Claude Code switches between screen modes during long coding sessions.
actionable_steps: Add 'export CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1' to your shell profile (.bashrc, .zshrc, etc.)
Restart your terminal or run 'source ~/.bashrc' to apply the change
Launch Claude Code to verify flicker-free rendering is active

tips.headline: Use defer permission in PreToolUse hooks to pause headless sessions
tips.summary: You can now pause headless Claude Code sessions at tool calls and resume them later with permission evaluation. This allows for better control over automated workflows that need human approval.
actionable_steps: Set up a PreToolUse hook in your Claude Code configuration
Return 'defer' as the permission decision in the hook
Resume the session using `claude-code -p --resume` command
The hook will re-evaluate the tool call upon resumption

tips.headline: Use /powerup command to learn Claude Code features interactively
tips.summary: Claude Code v2.1.90 introduced the /powerup command that provides interactive lessons with animated demos to help you learn Claude Code features. This is particularly useful for new users who want to quickly understand the tool's capabilities through hands-on tutorials.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to version 2.1.90 or later
Type `/powerup` in the Claude Code interface
Follow the interactive lessons and animated demos to learn features

tips.headline: Use _meta annotation to prevent large MCP tool results from being truncated
tips.summary: Claude Code now supports preserving large tool results (like database schemas) up to 500K characters by adding a special metadata annotation. This prevents important data from being cut off during processing.
actionable_steps: Add `_meta["anthropic/maxResultSizeChars"]` annotation to your MCP tool result
Set the value to your desired character limit (up to 500,000)
Test with large results like database schemas to verify they pass through completely

tips.headline: Use forceRemoteSettingsRefresh policy to ensure fresh configuration on startup
tips.summary: This setting forces Claude Code CLI to fetch the latest remote managed settings before starting and exits if the fetch fails. This ensures your CLI always runs with the most current configuration and prevents running with stale settings that might cause issues.
actionable_steps: Open your Claude Code CLI configuration
Add the policy setting `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh: true`
Restart the CLI to verify it blocks startup until fresh settings are fetched

tips.headline: Enable Amazon Bedrock support with Mantle integration
tips.summary: Claude Code v2.1.94 added support for Amazon Bedrock through Mantle integration. This allows you to use Claude Code with Amazon's Bedrock service instead of the default API endpoints, potentially offering better performance or compliance for enterprise users.
actionable_steps: Set the environment variable CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE=1 in your system or terminal
Restart Claude Code to apply the new configuration
Verify the connection is working by running a test query

tips.headline: Set up Google Vertex AI integration using the interactive wizard
tips.summary: Claude Code v2.1.98 introduced a guided setup wizard that simplifies connecting to Google Vertex AI. This eliminates manual configuration steps and reduces authentication errors by walking you through GCP setup, project selection, and credential verification.
actionable_steps: Open Claude Code and go to the login screen
Select '3rd-party platform' option
Follow the interactive Google Vertex AI setup wizard
Complete GCP authentication, project and region configuration, and credential verification as prompted

tips.headline: Use `/team-onboarding` command to generate teammate ramp-up guides
tips.summary: Claude Code can automatically create onboarding documentation for new team members based on your local usage patterns. This saves time creating training materials and ensures consistency in how team members learn your workflows.
actionable_steps: Update to Claude Code v2.1.101 or later
Run the `/team-onboarding` command in your Claude Code interface
Review the generated ramp-up guide and customize as needed
Share the guide with new team members

tips.headline: Use the path parameter with EnterWorktree to switch between git worktrees
tips.summary: The EnterWorktree tool now accepts a path parameter that lets you switch into existing worktrees of your current repository. This makes it easier to work with multiple branches or feature development in parallel without switching repositories.
actionable_steps: Identify the worktree path you want to switch to in your current repository
Use the EnterWorktree tool with the path parameter: `EnterWorktree(path="/path/to/your/worktree")`
Verify you're in the correct worktree by checking the current branch or directory

tips.headline: Use ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H to extend prompt cache duration
tips.summary: Setting this environment variable enables 1-hour prompt cache TTL instead of the default, which can reduce API costs and improve response times for longer coding sessions. This works across API key, Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry deployments.
actionable_steps: Set the environment variable ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=true in your system or deployment configuration
Restart Claude Code to apply the new caching setting
Monitor your usage to verify extended caching is working
